turn_text: I have been excited about working on in the last couple of years deals with the international aspects of cannabis. In 2019, I went to the United Nations for kind of their interim discussion on international drug policy. I chair the Trade Subcommittee for the Ways and Means Committee. And we have some interesting opportunities in terms of cannabis in the marketplace, interstate, and in-trust state. We now have North America, the potential of a North American cannabis zone. Canada has fully legal and of course you folks have been pioneers in that. Mexico has gone fully legal and we're watching the momentum build for the same thing in the United States. Having a North American unified market gives opportunities for product development, for research, for meeting the needs of customers in a way that I think is really exciting. And in terms of intra trade in the United States, as soon as we can get legal, having an opportunity to trade cannabis across state borders. One of the problems we have right now getting rid of the black market in terms of the success of various companies. We have a cannabis imbalance. I come from a region that produces an awful lot of high quality cannabis recognized internationally. But there's a surplus and there's no easy way to dispose of it and it invites some people to be involved with the gray market. When we can trade that across state lines, we can balance supply and demand. It's better for the industry. It's better for consumers and it is better for law enforcement. And those objectives in terms of a North America cannabis zone and being able to freely market cannabis across state lines are some of the first things we're going to do when everything is fully legal and I hope that happens within the year.
